title: 3,500 hospital beds added, but 40 lakh patients treated on floors
excerpt: The prime minister told parliament of the bed shortage and promised to push for a government hospital in Rangabali, home to about 400,000 people.
content:
About 3,500 hospital beds have been added across the country in recent months, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman told parliament on Wednesday (18 November), The Financial Express reported, citing BSS. He said about 40 lakh (4 million) patients had been treated on floors and verandas because of the shortage of beds.

He was answering a question on bed shortages from Syed Zainul Abedin, MP for Dhaka-4. ABM Mosharraf Hossain, MP for Patuakhali-4, said Rangabali upazila has about 400,000 people and no government hospital; the prime minister said he would instruct the health minister.

Why it matters

With patients treated on floors and no government hospital in Rangabali, remote coastal communities depend on referral and outreach services, where NGO health programmes often fill gaps.

What to watch

Where the new beds are and whether staff are hired to run them, and any budget for a Rangabali hospital.
